title: Defect manifest
description: A benchmark corpus and its hidden answer key. Each planted defect records its class, location, severity and the probe that triggers it, so reviewer recall and precision are measurable per class rather than as one number. The manifest is never materialized into the worktree a run sees: a corpus whose answer key is readable measures nothing.

archetype.description: The archetype from docs/benchmark-domains.md this task instantiates.

tier.description: A deterministic oracle, B hybrid, C weak. The tier decides which flow can score it.

seed_path.description: The tree materialized into the benchmark repository. Everything outside it stays hidden.

defect_class.description: 1-10 from the base taxonomy in docs/test-charter.md, 11-20 from the domain extensions in docs/benchmark-domains.md.

location.description: The path the defect lives in, optionally with :line. Scoring matches a finding to a defect by path.

triggering_probe.description: The check that exposes it. A planted defect no probe can expose is not a defect, it is an opinion.

probe_path.description: A script, relative to the corpus root, that decides whether this defect is still present in a candidate. Run as `<interpreter> <probe_path> <task directory inside the candidate>`; it must print exactly one line, DEFECT_PRESENT or DEFECT_ABSENT, and exit zero. Anything else is INDETERMINATE and is reported as such, never folded into a recall figure. Without one, a defect the worker fixed and a defect every reviewer missed both score zero and cannot be told apart.

probe_caveat.description: Where the probe's verdict is a heuristic rather than a decision. Prose defects have no executable oracle; saying so beside the probe is what keeps the number honest.

survives.description: What this defect is known to survive, which is why it is worth planting.
